content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation on § 21.1 (LOL-CAP).**

- **Problem:** The cap sat at one month of Fees actually paid — below the fallback floor (12 months) and inside walk-away territory — and "without exception" nullified the Excluded Claims regime in § 21.3, pulling indemnities, confidentiality, data protection/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement inside an illusory cap.
- **Cure (single surgical replace):** § 21.1 now reads "Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed the greater of Fees paid or payable in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000."
- **Already met (untouched):** mutuality of the cap (§ 21.1), mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages (§ 21.2), and Customer's payment obligations not being damages (§ 21.3) — so no additional language was added.

Submitted (final). Deviation on §§ 21.1 and 21.3, cured at the preferred level with two surgical replaces:

1. **§ 21.1** — "Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed the greater of Fees paid or payable in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000." Replaces the one-month, "without exception" cap so the § 21.3 Excluded Claims (confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) are genuinely uncapped.
2. **§ 21.3 final sentence** — "Customer's payment obligations for undisputed amounts due under this Agreement, including Fees, taxes, expenses and interest, are not damages and are not limited by this Section." This now reaches Customer's payment obligations as a whole (defined "Fees" omits taxes, expenses, interest and implementation charges) while retaining the Customer-favourable "undisputed" qualifier.

§ 21.2's mutual indirect/consequential exclusion and direct-damages sentence, and the Excluded Claims list itself, are preserved verbatim; no ancillary or non-element terms were added.

system.text:
You are an independent verifier of one proposed customer-side contract redline in a fresh context.
Treat the preferred and fallback positions as separate atomic checklists. Evaluate the operative rendered language, not the drafter's confidence or margin comment. Copy every supplied element string exactly into the corresponding output item, assess both levels, and return met, not_met, or cannot_tell with concise textual evidence. A conditional element is met when its stated condition does not apply, but explain why.

Apply rule boundaries: voluntary use of one Vendor interface is not a sole-supplier promise when Customer remains free to use alternatives; a disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic is MFN rather than exclusivity unless alternatives remain prohibited after compliance; natural-term non-renewal is evaluated under RENEWAL, not as mid-term T4C; an unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right. An auto-renewal clause permitting either party to terminate on notice does not make Vendor termination term-end-only unless the termination effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. A broad Vendor right to distribute, resell, independently exploit Customer Data, or use it for the wider "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" defeats the solely-to-provide-the-Services element even if ownership nominally remains with Customer. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer remains service delivery. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not itself a standing Vendor licence.

Fail intent if a Customer-only successor or licence-transfer element is implemented by granting Vendor a new assignment exception. A Customer Data insurance trigger must cover every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer, not merely selected named data types. Cosmetic deletion or paraphrase of words outside the target elements fails minimality.

For ASSIGN fallback, any retained no-consent non-successor exception—including a mutual affiliate exception—defeats "Other assignments require consent." Under LICENSE, resolve whether Customer already includes affiliates and fail minimality for duplicate coverage. A grant to an affiliate ordinarily permits use through its authorized personnel; a separate personnel/access edit is unnecessary unless retained language expressly contradicts the new grant. A broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause is non-minimal when a direct "without Vendor approval" transfer permission will do.

The redline is position-complete when every element at either the preferred level or the fallback level is met. Do not mark a level complete if an element is omitted, merely promised in the comment, internally inconsistent, or depends on an undefined trigger. Deterministic regexes are evidence; inspect their result in substance as well as mechanically.

Minimal means the proposal changes only what is needed to reach one complete level, retains favourable existing language, avoids duplicating operative terms, and adds no requirement outside the chosen checklist. Treat model-language extras as extras: survival tails, at-own-expense language, additional damages categories, procedures, or boilerplate fail minimality unless a selected element requires them. For a missing clause, a concise insertion can be minimal even though all its words are new. Preserves intent means unrelated allocation, timing, remedies, references, and commercial mechanics survive without contradiction; fail intent if an edit leaves an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence.

Read nouns, modifiers, temporal anchors, amounts, bases, scope, and party direction literally. Do not infer "pro rata" merely from a refund that covers a post-termination period. Do not equate broader "all amounts paid or payable" with "fees paid or payable", "the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to a claim" with "the 12 months preceding the claim", or a deadline running from a request with one running from termination. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief preserves an otherwise exclusive merits forum; a broader alternate forum does not. A "no field-of-use restriction" result is not complete while an exclusive Vendor right prevents Customer use of its own product or brand. Fail minimality when a fallback proposal exceeds its numeric threshold without necessity. A no-liquidated-damages result must be unconditional and leave no retained formula, instalment, or contingent payment mechanic. Treat removal of any word outside the chosen elements—even a Customer-favourable restriction—as a minimality failure. Do not infer an omitted element from general commercial context.

For a liability cap, resolve the definition used by any Customer-payment carve-out. Language excluding only a narrowly defined subset of Fees does not cover Customer payment obligations as a whole. Treat explanatory examples added to an otherwise complete formula as non-minimal.

For T4C, treat "in whole or in part" as surplus unless the selected checklist and an actual Order Form or partial-termination structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the stated assistance period must apply after every covered expiry or termination; a request condition tied only to anticipated expiry does not suffice. Certified deletion must occur after data return. For WARRANTY fallback, do not treat reports, outputs, or services as software merely because they conform to a manual; require an express software-to-documentation warranty unless the contract defines the item as software.

Give actionable reasons. If an element is not met, name the exact defect the drafter must repair in operative language.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule and exact checklists:
ID: LOL-CAP
Title: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
Kind: parametric
Summary: Liability must be capped for both parties at a meaningful amount, with standard carve-outs.
Severity: critical
Category: liability
Position — preferred:
Mutual cap equal to the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000; mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages; carve-outs (uncapped) for breach of confidentiality, data protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes.

Position — fallback:
Mutual cap of 12 months' fees; carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

Position — walk-away:
Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside the cap with no super-cap.

Detection guidance:
Find the limitation-of-liability, exclusion-of-damages and any "aggregate liability" language, including language hidden in warranty or indemnity sections. Determine: does a cap exist; what is the basis (fixed amount, months of fees, fees "paid" vs "paid or payable"); is it mutual or one-sided; which obligations are carved out. Resolve defined terms ("Fees", "Losses", "Claims") — a cap on "Fees" defined as a small set-up fee is illusory. A one-way cap that protects only the Vendor, or language stating the Customer's liability is unlimited, is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Edit the existing sentence(s); do not rewrite the section. Change the basis to 12 months' fees, make the cap mutual, and add one carve-out sentence. If Customer is uncapped, add Customer to the cap. Comment: state the position and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Model language:
Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.

You are in-house counsel producing a concise Markdown issues memo from verified findings.
Include: Executive summary; a Markdown table of findings with severity, rule, status and section; Walk-away items; Next steps.
Never invent a section reference or legal conclusion. Use only supplied findings.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Document: MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT

Findings:
[{"id":"f-indemn-24c442f6","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 20 INDEMNIFICATION 20.1 Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services.","rationale":"Section 20 contains only a one-way, unlimited Customer indemnity for Vendor covering \"every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services\", and no Vendor indemnity appears anywhere in the Agreement (Sections 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 merely presuppose indemnified claims). That is walk-away territory: no Vendor IP indemnity at all plus a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services, so it fails both the fallback and preferred positions. We therefore add Vendor's defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement, Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused unauthorised access to Customer Data and Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with notice, control-of-defence and cooperation mechanics, and narrow Customer's indemnity to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law. Noted but not separately flagged: Section 9.3 cross-refers to remedies \"required by Section 20.5\", which does not exist in the current draft; if Copperleaf prefers the fallback structure we can instead add the usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications), procure/modify/replace/refund remedies as Section 20.5, and a 3× annual fees super-cap.","proposal":"Add Vendor defence/indemnity (IP, breach of law, data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with notice, control and cooperation, and narrow Customer's indemnity.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ip-6135bee2","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 14.1 As between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services. No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer.","rationale":"The IP package meets our preferred position. § 14.2 gives us ownership of each Deliverable created specifically for us and contains Vendor's present assignment of all worldwide right, title and interest (plus equivalent assignments from its personnel). § 14.3 confirms Vendor retains only Vendor Technology (defined in § 1.8 as its pre-existing technology, excluding Customer Data and IP we owned before the Effective Date), and routes embedded Vendor Technology to the § 13.2 licence, which is perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free and fully paid, with modification and derivative-work rights for our business. § 14.1 confirms we own all Customer Data and that no right transfers to Vendor beyond a limited right to process it solely to provide, secure, support and improve the Services for us — service delivery, not independent exploitation — reinforced by § 15.1 (processing only on our documented instructions; no sale, advertising, data combination or model training without our express written consent). § 14.4 creates no joint ownership absent a separate signed instrument identifying exploitation rights, and preserves our unrestricted right to use our own feedback. Minor points noted but not flagged: § 14.2 conditions Deliverable ownership on payment of the applicable Fees, and § 15.1 includes an \"as permitted by this Agreement\" processing hook. Section 13.1's revocable Services licence is a LICENSE-rule issue and is not double-flagged here.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-99743d6a","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 21.1 Each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed Fees actually paid in the one month preceding the event, without exception.","rationale":"Section 21.1 caps each Party at one month of Fees actually paid — below the fallback floor of 12 months' fees and inside walk-away territory — and \"without exception\" overrides the Excluded Claims regime in 21.3, pulling indemnities, confidentiality, data protection/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement inside an illusory cap. We re-base the cap in 21.1 to the greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable measured to the claim and USD 1,000,000, and replace \"without exception\" with the \"Except for Excluded Claims\" hook so the carve-outs genuinely operate. The retained payment carve-out reached only \"undisputed Fees for conforming Services\", and defined \"Fees\" (cl. 1.5) excludes taxes, reimbursable expenses, interest and any one-time implementation charge, so we extend it to Customer's payment obligations for undisputed amounts due, expressly including taxes, expenses and interest, while preserving the Customer-favourable \"undisputed\" qualifier. Section 21.2's mutual damages exclusion is untouched.","proposal":"Re-base the cap to the greater of 12 months' Fees and USD 1,000,000, remove \"without exception\", and make all of Customer's payment obligations fall outside damages subject to the cap.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-assign-77a5f935","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.","rationale":"Section 24 meets the preferred position. § 24.1 lets Customer assign to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets without Vendor's consent (notice only). § 24.2 bars Vendor assignment, delegation of material performance, or transfer by change of control without Customer's prior written consent, with the reasonableness standard running in Customer's favour, and bars assignment to a direct Customer competitor. § 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any termination, suspension, repricing, acceleration or service-reduction right on Customer's change of control, so the walk-away trigger is absent. § 13.3 reinforces Customer's licence-transfer right. Only minor wording points fall short of ideal drafting — the competitor bar is qualified by \"without Customer's consent\" (immaterial, since no Vendor assignment is permitted without our consent at all) and the § 24.2 reasonableness standard omits \"conditioned or delayed\" (supplied for other assignments in § 24.3). These are noted, not redlined.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-75577550","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 2.2 Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.","rationale":"The first Section 2.2 imposes a full-term sole-and-exclusive-supplier obligation on Customer for hosted analytics services, with no category limit, no 12-month cap, and no automatic exit for service-level or delivery-date failures — walk-away territory under the rule, well short of the fallback. Section 12.3's statement that Customer has made no exclusivity commitment is countervailing but directly contradicted by Section 2.2, so the contradictory operative grant must be fixed rather than relied upon. We therefore made the appointment non-exclusive, achieving the preferred position with the shortest edit and aligning Section 2.2 with Section 12.3.","proposal":"Convert the sole-and-exclusive-provider commitment into a non-exclusive appointment with no sole-supplier obligation.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-3306e643","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor. Customer owes Fees only for conforming Services provided through the effective termination date, and Vendor shall promptly refund prepaid Fees allocable to the period after that date. Vendor has no corresponding convenience-termination right during a committed term.","rationale":"We searched the Agreement for liquidated damages, penalties, early-termination or cancellation charges, minimum fees on termination, and acceleration of Fees, and found none payable by Customer. On Customer's convenience termination (§ 9.4) Customer owes Fees only for conforming Services rendered to the termination date, with a refund of prepaid Fees; § 27.3 lets Customer terminate for prolonged force majeure \"without penalty\"; and § 7.3 bars interest on amounts found not due. This meets the preferred position (no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer), so no redline is warranted. Note for completeness: the § 2.1 take-or-pay minimum commitment is a volume commitment rather than a liquidated damages or penalty amount and is addressed under the minimum-commitment rule; we do not double-flag it here.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-license-ba1bc9f1","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 13.1 Vendor grants Customer alone a non-transferable licence, revocable at Vendor's sole discretion, to use the Services without Affiliates or contractors.","rationale":"Section 13.1, the grant for the subscription Services, is walk-away territory: it runs to \"Customer alone\", expressly excludes Affiliates and contractors with no path to add them, is non-transferable, and is revocable at Vendor's sole discretion. Sections 13.2 and 13.3 give us the preferred position for the paid-up software licence (perpetual, irrevocable, Affiliates and contractor support) and a transfer right to an Affiliate or successor in connection with an assignment permitted by Section 24 (which under 24.1 includes a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent), but 13.1 contradicts those protections for the Services licence. The single edit to 13.1 extends the grant to our Affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf and replaces at-will revocation with the uncured material breach standard already in 13.3, and deleting \"non-transferable\" removes the conflict with the 13.3 transfer right. No separate personnel or access clause prohibits contractor use, so no collateral change is needed.","proposal":"Extend the Services licence in 13.1 to Affiliates and contractors and remove Vendor's at-will revocation and the non-transferability bar.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mincommit-953097f3","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.","rationale":"Section 2.1 imposes a three-year, USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay commitment expressly \"without reduction or termination rights\" — walk-away territory under MINCOMMIT and a clear failure of the fallback (no 12-month limit, no 30-day reduction right, no true-up mechanic; a take-or-pay shortfall is a penalty). It also conflicts with § 12.3 (Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment) and § 9.4 (Customer's convenience-termination right, under which Customer owes Fees only for conforming Services provided through the effective date). We therefore replace the commitment with the preferred position: no minimum purchase or volume commitment, with payment only for usage or ordered Services, which is consistent with § 7.1's Order Form fee mechanic.","proposal":"Delete the three-year take-or-pay and confirm no minimum commitment; Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-768576ee","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.","rationale":"§ 12.4 imposes on Customer a non-compete of undefined scope (\"any product or service that competes with Vendor\"), worldwide, running for 24 months after the term, with no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions. That is walk-away territory under this rule (post-term non-compete longer than 12 months and undefined scope) and fails every fallback element. It also directly contradicts § 12.3, in which \"Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.\" No other clause imposes a competitive or field-of-use restriction on Customer (§ 13.4 is ordinary acceptable-use). We therefore take the preferred position and convert § 12.4 into an express confirmation that Customer is free to compete, aligning it with § 12.3.","proposal":"Convert § 12.4's 24-month post-term worldwide non-compete into an express confirmation that Customer is free to compete.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-t4c-572bf3ca","ruleId":"T4C","ruleTitle":"Termination for convenience","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 9.4 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor. Customer owes Fees only for conforming Services provided through the effective termination date, and Vendor shall promptly refund prepaid Fees allocable to the period after that date. Vendor has no corresponding convenience-termination right during a committed term.","rationale":"Section 9.4 satisfies the preferred position in full: Customer may terminate the Agreement or any Order Form for convenience on thirty days' written notice, Vendor must promptly refund prepaid Fees allocable to the post-termination period (a pro-rata refund), and Vendor is expressly denied any corresponding convenience-termination right during a committed term. No other termination provision (§§ 9.1–9.3, 9.5, 10.1–10.2, 27.3) grants Vendor a convenience right, and § 8.2 non-renewal is Customer-controlled with a Vendor reminder obligation, so it is a renewal mechanic rather than a Vendor mid-term convenience right. No early-termination fee or penalty appears anywhere. The only tension is § 2.1's take-or-pay commitment \"without reduction or termination rights,\" which sits with the minimum-commitment rule rather than T4C and is not flagged twice here. No redline proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-transition-3e7ce3f7","ruleId":"TRANSITION","ruleTitle":"Post-termination transition assistance and data return","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 11.1 Immediately on termination Vendor shall discontinue all assistance and permanently delete Customer Data without offering an export or migration support.","rationale":"Section 11.1 is walk-away territory: it denies any transition assistance and mandates immediate permanent deletion of Customer Data with no export or migration support, so the fallback (90 days of assistance; export within 30 days) is not met and 11.1 also contradicts 11.2 and 11.3. Sections 11.2 and 11.3 already supply the machine-readable return format and officer-certified deletion after Customer confirms return, so the shortest complete cure is to replace 11.1 with an expiry-or-termination trigger, up to six months' assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, and return of Customer Data within thirty days, reaching the preferred position without disturbing 11.2 or 11.3.","proposal":"Replace Section 11.1's immediate cessation/deletion with six months of transition assistance at then-current rates and return of Customer Data within thirty days of expiry or termination.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-audit-ff057a57","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer. An audit will be conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality.","rationale":"§ 22.1 caps audits at once in any twelve-month period, requires thirty days' prior written notice, confines audits to normal business hours, and requires an off-site (where practicable) audit by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality. § 22.2 puts audit cost on Vendor unless the audit establishes underpayment exceeding five percent, and bars Vendor and its auditor from direct access to Customer systems (and from unrelated Customer Data, privileged material and third-party confidential information). This meets every element of our preferred position, not merely the fallback, and § 22.3 additionally treats findings as Customer Confidential Information. No other audit, inspection or verification right binding Customer exists in the document (§ 23 carries no operative text). No redline needed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-govlaw-dae1813e","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 28.1 This Agreement and each dispute arising from it are governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-law principles. The United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods does not apply.","rationale":"Section 28.1 selects New York law and Section 28.2 gives the state and federal courts in New York County exclusive jurisdiction, with an irrevocable submission to personal jurisdiction and waiver of venue objections. The only carve-out is the customary right to seek temporary injunctive relief elsewhere to protect confidential information or IP, which does not defeat the exclusive merits forum. No arbitration provision (foreign-seated or otherwise) appears anywhere in the document; Section 28.3's pre-filing executive escalation is a short good-faith meeting that expressly does not delay urgent relief or limitations-period filings, so it does not displace the court forum. This sits at our preferred position, so no redline is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mfn-e6e5a72a","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.","rationale":"The Agreement imposes no most-favoured-nation or most-favoured-customer obligation on Customer. Section 12.3 affirmatively confirms that Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment, and the pricing provisions (§ 7.1 fixed Fees; § 8.3 capped renewal uplift) impose no duty on Customer to extend Vendor terms given to third parties or to match third-party offers. This meets the preferred position (no Customer MFN obligation); no redline is required. Separate exclusivity (§ 2.2) and non-compete (§ 12.4) issues are outside this rule and are addressed under their own playbook rules.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-nosolicit-d2128ed3","ruleId":"NOSOLICIT","ruleTitle":"Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.","rationale":"Searches for \"solicit\", \"hire\", \"employ or engage\", \"induce\", \"recruit\", \"personnel\" and \"restrictive covenant\", plus a sweep of Section 12 and Section 30.1, return no non-solicitation or no-hire covenant binding either Party. Section 12.3 affirmatively preserves Customer's freedom to hire any person who responds to general recruitment and records that Customer has made no no-hire commitment; Section 30.1 is only an independent-contractor provision. This meets the preferred position (no non-solicit on Customer), so no redline is proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-renewal-33e30b33","ruleId":"RENEWAL","ruleTitle":"Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.","rationale":"The renewal bargain meets the preferred position in full. § 8.2 provides automatic renewal in successive twelve-month periods (no multi-year evergreen), a Customer opt-out on thirty days' written notice (within the 30-day preferred limit), and a Vendor reminder at least sixty days before renewal, with the opt-out deadline extended if the reminder is not sent. § 8.3 caps renewal increases to recurring Fees at the lesser of US CPI-U over the preceding twelve months and three percent, with ninety days' notice and no increase on prepaid periods. Because every conditional automatic-renewal element is satisfied, mutual written agreement is not required. No redline is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-warranty-7117be83","ruleId":"WARRANTY","ruleTitle":"Performance warranty and duration","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 19.1 Vendor warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards, this Agreement, and each Order Form. {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal Team 
**From:** In-house Counsel (Customer-side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of Vendor's Master Services Agreement draft 

---

## Executive Summary

We have completed our playbook review of the Master Services Agreement. Of the 19 rules assessed, **8 clauses deviate** from our positions and **11 are compliant**. The compliant set is genuinely strong: IP and Customer Data ownership (§§ 14.1–14.4, 13.2), assignment and change of control (§ 24), Customer-side termination for convenience (§ 9.4), audit rights (§ 22), renewal mechanics (§ 8.2–8.3), governing law and venue (§ 28), Vendor insurance (§ 18) and the absence of any MFN, non-solicit or liquidated damages burden on Customer all meet our preferred position.

The deviations, however, are concentrated in the most consequential commercial and risk provisions, and several sit squarely in walk-away territory:

- **No Vendor indemnity exists anywhere in the Agreement**, paired with a one-way, unlimited Customer indemnity for Vendor covering "every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services" (§ 20.1).
- **The liability cap is one month of Fees actually paid, "without exception"** (§ 21.1), which is below our floor and neutralises the Excluded Claims regime in § 21.3.
- **A three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay commitment with no reduction or termination rights** (§ 2.1), a **full-term sole-and-exclusive supplier obligation** (§ 2.2), and a **24-month worldwide post-term non-compete** (§ 12.4) — each of which directly contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no such commitments.
- **§ 11.1 requires immediate cessation of all assistance and permanent deletion of Customer Data** with no export or migration path, contradicting §§ 11.2 and 11.3.
- The **Services licence in § 13.1** runs to "Customer alone", excludes Affiliates and contractors, and is revocable at Vendor's sole discretion — inconsistent with the paid-up licence protections in §§ 13.2–13.3.
- The **conformity warranty period is fifteen days** (§ 19.2), below our 90-day fallback floor, and cuts off the § 19.4 remedies.

A notable feature of this draft is internal inconsistency: § 12.3 disclaims exactly the exclusivity, minimum-volume and non-compete commitments that §§ 2.1, 2.2 and 12.4 impose, and § 11.1 conflicts with §§ 11.2–11.3. Several of our edits simply align the operative grants with Vendor's own acknowledgements. We also note that § 9.3 cross-refers to remedies "required by Section 20.5", a section that does not exist in the current draft.

---

## Findings Table

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 20 / § 20.1 (with §§ 19.4, 21.3, 30.5) |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Deviation | § 21.1 (with §§ 21.2, 21.3, cl. 1.5) |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | §§ 14.1–14.4, 13.2, 15.1 |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Deviation | § 2.2 (contradicts § 12.3) |
| High | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase / volume commitments | Deviation | § 2.1 (contradicts §§ 12.3, 9.4) |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 (contradicts § 12.3) |
| High | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | Deviation | § 11.1 (contradicts §§ 11.2, 11.3) |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 13.1 (cf. §§ 13.2, 13.3) |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | §§ 24.1–24.4, 13.3 |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § 9.4 (with §§ 27.3, 7.3) |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9.4 (with §§ 9.1–9.3, 9.5, 10.1–10.2, 8.2, 27.3) |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 19.2 (cf. §§ 19.1, 19.3, 19.4) |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | §§ 22.1–22.3 |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | §§ 28.1–28.3 |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | § 12.3 (with §§ 7.1, 8.3) |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees | Compliant | § 12.3 (with § 30.1) |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | §§ 8.2, 8.3 |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | §§ 18.1, 18.2 |

---

## Walk-Away Items

The following findings were assessed as falling in walk-away territory under the playbook. Each must be resolved before signature.

1. **Indemnification (§ 20.1) — Critical.** No Vendor IP indemnity exists anywhere in the Agreement, combined with an unlimited one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor covering Vendor's own services. This fails both the fallback and preferred positions.

2. **Liability cap (§ 21.1) — Critical.** A one-month cap on Fees *actually paid* sits below the 12-month fallback floor, and "without exception" overrides § 21.3, pulling indemnities, confidentiality, data protection and security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement inside an illusory cap.

3. **Minimum commitment (§ 2.1) — High.** A three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay expressly "without reduction or termination rights": no 12-month limit, no 30-day reduction right, no true-up, and a shortfall that operates as a penalty.

4. **Exclusivity (§ 2.2) — High.** A full-term sole-and-exclusive-provider obligation with no category limit, no 12-month cap and no automatic exit for service-level or delivery-date failures.

5. **Non-compete (§ 12.4) — High.** A worldwide, 24-month post-term non-compete of undefined scope, with no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions.

6. **Transition and data return (§ 11.1) — High.** Immediate cessation of all assistance and permanent deletion of Customer Data with no export or migration support.

7. **Services licence (§ 13.1) — High.** Grant to "Customer alone", excluding Affiliates and contractors with no path to add them, non-transferable, and revocable at Vendor's sole discretion.

---

## Next Steps

1. **Issue the redlined draft** covering the eight deviations, with the following proposals:
   - **§ 20:** add Vendor defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement, Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused unauthorised access to Customer Data, and Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with notice, control-of-defence and cooperation mechanics; narrow Customer's indemnity to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
   - **§ 21.1:** re-base the cap to the greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable measured to the claim and USD 1,000,000; replace "without exception" with an "Except for Excluded Claims" hook; extend the payment carve-out to Customer's payment obligations for undisputed amounts due, expressly including taxes, expenses and interest (retaining the Customer-favourable "undisputed" qualifier). § 21.2 untouched.
   - **§ 2.1:** delete the take-or-pay and confirm no minimum purchase or volume commitment; Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services, consistent with § 7.1.
   - **§ 2.2:** convert to a non-exclusive appointment with no sole-supplier obligation, aligning with § 12.3.
   - **§ 12.4:** convert to an express confirmation that Customer is free to compete, aligning with § 12.3.
   - **§ 11.1:** replace immediate cessation and deletion with an expiry-or-termination trigger, up to six months' transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, and return of Customer Data within thirty days — leaving §§ 11.2 and 11.3 (machine-readable return format; officer-certified deletion) intact.
   - **§ 13.1:** extend the grant to our Affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf, replace at-will revocation with the uncured material breach standard already in § 13.3, and delete "non-transferable" to remove the conflict with the § 13.3 transfer right.
   - **§ 19.2:** extend the conformity period to ninety (90) days, apply it to software as well as Deliverables, and delete the fifteen-day cut-off of correction and refund obligations.

2. **Prepare fallback positions** where sensible. On indemnity, if Vendor prefers the fallback structure we can accept the usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications), procure/modify/replace/refund remedies inserted as § 20.5, and a 3× annual fees super-cap. On warranty, § 19.2 as redlined lands at the fallback; we are not pressing the preferred twelve-month software period.

3. **Flag the drafting defect** in § 9.3, which cross-refers to remedies "required by Section 20.5" — a provision that does not exist in the current draft. Our indemnity redline can supply it.

4. **Raise the internal inconsistencies** with Vendor as a package: § 12.3 disclaims the very exclusivity, minimum-volume and non-compete commitments imposed by §§ 2.2, 2.1 and 12.4, and § 11.1 contradicts §§ 11.2–11.3. Aligning the operative grants with Vendor's own acknowledgements should be presented as a clean-up rather than a negotiation.

5. **Confirm no re-trade on compliant provisions.** We will not reopen IP (§ 14), assignment (§ 24), convenience termination (§ 9.4), audit (§ 22), renewal (§ 8.2–8.3), governing law (§ 28) or insurance (§ 18). Minor sub-elements noted for the record only: the § 14.2 payment condition on Deliverable ownership; the § 15.1 "as permitted by this Agreement" processing hook; the § 24.2 reasonableness standard omitting "conditioned or delayed"; and the § 24 competitor bar qualified by "without Customer's consent".

6. **Escalate for business sign-off** on the walk-away items, in particular §§ 2.1, 2.2 and 12.4, which have direct commercial and strategic consequences beyond legal risk allocation."}
